pharm: Irreversible covalent inhibitor of fibroblast growth factor receptors 1 through 4 (FGFR1-4); blocks FGFR signaling to inhibit tumor growth in FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement-positive cholangiocarcinoma
quick: 20 mg orally once daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity
Take with or without food at the same time each day
Can cause fetal harm; avoid - use effective contraception
Do not breastfeed during and for 1 week after the last dose
No adjustment in mild-moderate; not studied in severe
No adjustment in mild; not studied in moderate-severe
No specific interaction; limit due to additive effects
Ophthalmic exams, serum phosphate, LFTs, pregnancy status
summary: Futibatinib (Lytgobi) is an irreversible oral inhibitor of FGFR1-4 indicated for adults with previously treated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2 gene fusions or other rearrangements, as detected by an FDA-approved test. The dose is 20 mg once daily continuously until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Key risks include ocular toxicity with retinal pigment epithelial detachment (RPED), hyperphosphatemia with soft-tissue mineralization risk, stomatitis, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, nail toxicity, and embryo-fetal toxicity. It has no boxed warning.
indications: Treatment of adults with previously treated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2 gene fusions or other rearrangements, as detected by an FDA-approved test

dosage.t: Once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: Confirm FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement with an FDA-approved test before starting
Withhold for RPED, severe hyperphosphatemia, or other intolerable toxicity, then resume at reduced dose
Permanently discontinue if unable to tolerate 12 mg once daily

dosage.d: Initiate low-phosphate diet when phosphate >5.5 mg/dL; add phosphate-lowering therapy when >7 mg/dL
dosage.n: Withhold, reduce, or permanently discontinue for prolonged or severe hyperphosphatemia per labeling

admin: Take 20 mg (five 4 mg tablets) by mouth once daily at about the same time each day, with or without food
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush, chew, split, or dissolve
Obtain a comprehensive ophthalmologic exam including OCT before starting, every 2 months for the first 6 months, every 3 months thereafter, and urgently for any visual symptoms
Start a low-phosphate diet when serum phosphate exceeds 5.5 mg/dL and add phosphate-lowering therapy when it exceeds 7 mg/dL
If a dose is missed by more than 12 hours or vomiting occurs after a dose, skip it and take the next dose at the scheduled time
moa: Futibatinib binds covalently and irreversibly to the ATP-binding pocket of FGFR1, FGFR2, FGFR3, and FGFR4, inhibiting FGFR phosphorylation and downstream signaling through the RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK and PI3K/AKT pathways. Unlike reversible FGFR inhibitors, covalent binding maintains inhibition despite FGFR2 kinase-domain resistance mutations. In FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement-positive cholangiocarcinoma, blockade of constitutive FGFR signaling inhibits tumor cell proliferation and survival.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to futibatinib or any excipient
relative: Pre-existing retinal disorders or risk factors for retinal pigment epithelial detachment
Hyperphosphatemia or disorders predisposing to soft-tissue mineralization
Concomitant dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inducers
monitor: Visual symptoms and OCT findings for retinal pigment epithelial detachment
Skin, nails, and mucosa for stomatitis, hand-foot syndrome, and nail toxicity
Pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal findings, futibatinib can cause fetal harm including embryofetal mortality and malformations. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on the presence of futibatinib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild to moderate renal impairment. Futibatinib has not been studied in severe renal impairment; use with caution and monitor closely.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild hepatic impairment. Futibatinib has not been studied in moderate or severe hepatic impairment; use with caution if at all.

major: Dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) - substantially reduce futibatinib exposure; avoid concomitant use
Dual P-gp and moderate CYP3A inducers - may reduce futibatinib exposure; avoid where possible
moderate: Phosphate-increasing agents (e.g., vitamin D analogues, phosphate supplements) - worsen hyperphosphatemia; monitor phosphate
minor: No clinically meaningful effect of acid-reducing agents or CYP3A inhibitors requiring dose change per labeling
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; no clinically significant food effect. Maintain a low-phosphate diet when phosphate is elevated.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol due to additive constitutional and hepatic effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum phosphate and renal function; ophthalmologic exams with OCT for RPED; monitor liver function tests.

serious: Retinal pigment epithelial detachment (RPED) with vision changes
emergency: Sudden vision loss, flashing lights, or visual field changes (RPED) - seek urgent ophthalmology
Signs of severe hyperphosphatemia with muscle cramps or calcinosis - seek urgent care
Severe mouth sores preventing hydration or nutrition

monitoring: Comprehensive ophthalmologic exam with OCT before starting, every 2 months for 6 months, every 3 months thereafter, and urgently for visual symptoms
Serum phosphate at baseline and periodically; initiate low-phosphate diet and phosphate-lowering therapy per thresholds
Liver function tests and renal function periodically
Skin, nails, and oral mucosa for stomatitis, hand-foot syndrome, and nail toxicity
Pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential
counsel: Take five 4 mg tablets once a day at about the same time, with or without food; swallow whole
Report any vision changes such as blurred vision, flashing lights, or dark spots right away - you will need regular eye exams
Follow a low-phosphate diet and take phosphate-lowering medicine as prescribed when told your phosphate is high
Report mouth sores, painful red palms or soles, nail changes, or rash promptly
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed; tell your doctor about all other medicines, especially seizure medicines and St John's wort
pk: FGFR inhibition begins with first doses; tumor responses develop over weeks
Median plasma Tmax approximately 2 hours after oral dosing
Sustained target inhibition with once-daily dosing; steady state within about 1 week
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C permitted); protect from moisture
pearls: Irreversible covalent FGFR1-4 inhibitor - retains activity against some FGFR2 kinase-domain resistance mutations that limit reversible FGFR inhibitors
Requires documented FGFR2 fusion or other rearrangement by an FDA-approved test; indicated for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma after prior treatment
RPED can occur at any time - scheduled OCT surveillance plus urgent exam for any visual symptom
Hyperphosphatemia is an on-target class effect - manage early with diet and binders rather than stopping drug prematurely
Standard dose reductions are 20 mg to 16 mg to 12 mg; discontinue if 12 mg is not tolerated
missed: If you miss a dose of futibatinib by more than about 12 hours, or if you vomit after taking a dose, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific treatment for futibatinib overdose. Symptoms are not well defined but may reflect exaggerated adverse effects such as hyperphosphatemia, ocular toxicity, and mucocutaneous toxicity. Manage with supportive care, monitor serum phosphate, renal function, and vision, and provide ophthalmologic evaluation as indicated.
